News.title: Female biology teacher accused of sexually abusing six children and ‘forced one to watch Fifty Shades of Grey’
News.content:
SICK MISS Female biology teacher accused of sexually abusing six children and ‘forced one to watch Fifty Shades of Grey’

A BIOLOGY teacher has been accused of sexually abusing six children – including allegedly forcing one girl to watch Fifty Shades of Grey.

Maris Nichols, 25, was accused of sexually assaulting the same student twice in two weeks, before she was hit further charges relating to five more teens.





Nichols is accused of telling a female victim to watch the R-rated Fifty Shades of Grey films, according to an arrest warrant seen by the Daily Mail.

The document also claimed the teacher had sex with a student in the back seat of a truck.

She is also accused of sending nudes and explicit text messages to several teenage students, including two who were under the age of 16.

Nichols also allegedly described sex acts that she desired to the teens, which the warrant said included being “choked, screamed at, slapped and whipped”.



The science teacher allegedly told one teen to delete messages she had sent him and to lie if he was questioned about any sexual abuse.

She taught biology at Alexander High School in Douglasville in Georgia.

Nichols was first accused of having sex with a pupil in a cupboard between classrooms on April 23.

She then allegedly sexually abused the same student inside a parked Hummer.



Nichols was first hired as a football operations manager at the school in April 2023 but became a Biology teacher just one month later and continued in both roles, according to her LinkedIn.

After the disturbing allegations, the school suspended Nichols and wiped her profile from their website and launched an investigation.

Nichols was first arrested on a $40,000 bond earlier this month.



The alleged abuser, who is married with one child, was bailed out, then arrested for a second time on a $74,000 bond.

In a letter to parents after the first arrest, the Douglas County School System said: “Upon learning of the alleged misconduct, the district immediately launched an investigation.

“Student safety is the district’s highest priority.

“The alleged behavior is unacceptable and violates the professional standards all employees are required to uphold”.

A concerned local parent called the horrifying allegations “heartbreaking”.



Others told 11 Alive that Nichols gave their children very little help in class, and worried that their students would fall behind.

One unnamed parent said: “‘We’re not asking for special treatment. We are asking for transparency, accountability, and fairness.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Unfortunately, our concerns have repeatedly been met with resistance, limited communication, and a lack of meaningful reassurance that appropriate measures are being taken to protect all children involved, including our own.”

Nichols faces several charges of child molestation, grooming of a minor for a sexual offence, improper sexual contact by an employee and tampering with evidence.

News.title: Inside UK’s ‘benefits city’ as workers rage jobless parents are rinsing Starmer’s handouts to ‘trot off to Disneyland’
News.content:
AS the setting for the infamous reality TV show Benefits Street, Britain’s so-called ‘second city’ has long been the face of the nation’s spiralling welfare bill.

Now, fed-up workers in Birmingham have slammed the “unsustainable” situation after Labour’s scrapping of the two-child benefits cap was accused of “giving a green light” to brazen claimants.





New analysis of the latest Department for Work and Pensions data by The Sun revealed the areas where thousands of families are now entitled to significantly more taxpayer cash following the controversial policy change, which came into force last month.

And our investigation found that Birmingham leads the pack, with 17,990 families already on Universal Credit now eligible to claim extra cash because they have three or more children.

During our visit to the West Midlands city, many hard-grafting locals said they were furious that Prime Minister Keir Starmer‘s cap-lift has only furthered the sense “it’s not worth going to work anymore”.

While some welcomed the changes – insisting it would stop them “struggling to buy food” and having to live “day-by-by” – other locals argued the system is too open to abuse, with out-of-work parents openly telling them that their large broods of kids are their “safety net”.

This attitude was brazenly endorsed by one resident from the city’s ‘Benefits Street’ – the subject of a Channel 4 reality show – who said it was claimants’ “right” to get as much as they can from “exploiting the system”.

Locals in the city – recently named both the UK’s ‘sicknote’ and unemployment capital – have long felt left behind after enduring a near-440-day bin strike, which has seen six-foot mounds of festering rubbish pile the streets and led to rats “the size of cats”.

Brummies certainly made their voices clear in the May elections, with Labour losing 48 of their 65 seat majority at Birmingham City Council. Reform UK scooped 23 of them, followed by the Greens with 19, but there remains no party majority.

Alum Rock, three miles east of the city centre, risks becoming the face of the UK’s soaring child welfare payments, due to hosting 1,154 of Birmingham’s 17,990 families that already claim Universal Credit and have three or more children.



On the suburb’s bustling high street, we met retired 999 emergency call operator John Read, 72, who was angry that “slacker parents” take such high amounts “for doing nothing”.

“It’s atrocious, topsy turvy and not sustainable,” he said. “People going to work are paying for this through taxes while they’re struggling to afford their own bills.

“I’ve got about 14 nephews and nieces. Every one one of them is a hard-working grafter, and even they are now saying, ‘It’s not worth going to work anymore’. It’s shocking.

“If people can get free money for not working, they are going to do it. It’s human nature for some people, but politicians don’t realise because they live in a Westminster bubble.”



Former Labour member John says the party now “couldn’t run a jumble sale” and are “no longer for the working man”.

“Labour is unrecognisable,” he adds. “This current lot haven’t got their hands dirty a day in their lives, they all smell of lavender and wear Savile Row suits. They don’t represent us.”

Labour’s abolition of the two-child benefits cap came into effect on April 6.

If the two-child cap hadn’t been lifted, couples this year – aged over 25, with two or more kids, and claiming benefits – would receive up to £15,299 per year or £1,274 per month.



Now able to claim for extra offspring, the capped maximum sum is £22,020 per year or £1,835 per month in Birmingham. In London, it’s capped at £25,323 per year or £2,110 per month.

Not all will take the highest sum because Universal Credit payments are means-tested and include a range of allowances including housing, childcare, health issues, disabilities and carer support.

Six miles south-west of Alum Rock in Harborne, mum-of-four Lucie, 28, told us she’s extremely grateful for the extra handouts that have seen her child benefit payments double to £1,200 per month.

It means she is no longer “struggling to buy food”, can “actually live, not live day-by-by” and no longer has to rely on her “godsend mum” for money.

Labour ministers argue abolishing the two-child cap will lift 550,000 children out of poverty by the end of the Parliament and it has certainly been a lifeline for Lucie.



She told us she couldn’t wait to get back to work but admitted not everyone is like her, with some parents “taking the mick” because it is “so easy to get benefits and not have to do anything for it”.

She added: “Some people think, now they’re getting the extra money, that’s it’s the same ‘wage’ that they would get working part-time.

“I don’t think they have the mindset of going back to work anymore. Others have said it would be easier to have another kid than work because you get more money for it.”



It’s an approach deplored by many, including a nearby electrician – who declined to be named – who warned that if some claimants are “given an inch, they will take a mile”.

He added: “The system is so easily abused, that’s the problem. I don’t agree with it.

“I’ve worked hard ever since I was a kid, while people on benefits have the life of Riley. You see them going to Disneyland with their benefits. It’s not great is it?”

Former teacher Jacky Plotnek, 74, believes child benefits are essential due to the “pockets of extreme deprivation” in Birmingham – but also thinks people should not have kids if they cannot afford them.

She said: “We’re in a nanny state now – with school meals, breakfast clubs, children not ready for school, all of these things. Parents don’t have the skills that they used to have.”



On the possible £22,000-plus earnings, Jacky added: “That could have a negative effect on the way people view parenthood. It’s detrimental and the country can’t afford it, can we?”

Similarly, retired electrician Graham Leach, 77, told us: “People are being bought up with a ‘benefits attitude’, and it has got to stop. The country doesn’t make enough money to pay the benefits out.

“They think everything comes for free but it all comes at a cost – increases in tax, council tax, national insurance.

“I don’t mind benefits as a safety net, but there are people now receiving benefits who have never paid a penny into the system.

“And unscrupulous people could be having children to get more money. In the past people were grateful for a council house, now they expect it.”



Graham’s partner, Sandra Holloway, believes the abuse of the welfare state has turned the UK into “the silliest country of all”.

The retired hairdresser, 78, told of a well-educated dad, who couldn’t get a job, feeling relieved because his five kids were “his safety net” – referring to benefit payments.

Similarly, accountant Anam Hassan, 35, who moved from Pakistan to the UK nearly four years ago, argued unemployed parents “shouldn’t become a burden on the Government”.

The mum-of-one says: “Parents should be encouraged to find work, not manipulate the Government.

“Trying to increase your family to get more benefits is cheating, it’s not fair on hard-working parents like me.”



However, on James Turner Street, known for the docuseries Benefits Street – named due to 90 per cent of the neighbourhood claiming welfare payments – some people are more forgiving.

Local Vincent Gordon told us everyone should “see what they can get” from the Government and push for as much as possible.

The long-term street resident claimed: “It’s a natural reaction, people exploiting the system, but people should try to get more if they can.

“It’s your right to try to get more and if you can’t, at least you tried… some will get away with something, some will get away with nothing.”

Nearby resident Mohammed, 34, argued the public “shouldn’t worry” about the bulging benefits bill because “more money is being wasted on wars that have nothing to do with us”.



Mohammed admits the welfare system is “not perfect” but insists children should always be the nation’s focus – because they are future taxpayers.

“I know it doesn’t look good when you’re working and see someone at home doing nothing, but no child should go hungry,” he said.

“That child, who was supported by the government welfare system, could become 10 times better than his parents were.



“If a person has five kids and claims for them, those kids will all be paying taxes in the future so they will eventually be paying the money back.”

Conservative MP Helen Whately, the Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary, told us: “Labour scrapped the cap at a cost of more than £3billion a year, forcing working families to bear the cost.

“One in four workers now earn less than they’d get from welfare in Starmer’s Benefits Street Britain. Hardworking families across Birmingham know this is not fair.”

Welfare Secretary Pat McFadden said: “Children growing up in poverty are far more likely to leave school without qualifications and end up not in work or education as young adults, and we’re determined to break that cycle once and for all and give every child the best start in life.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Government spokesperson told us their Child Poverty Strategy would lift 550,000 kids out of poverty by 2030 and other welfare reforms will save “nearly £2billion by the end of the decade”.



They added: “Child poverty costs the country billions through pressure on public services and lost potential and with six in 10 of benefitting families having a parent in work, scrapping the two-child limit is an investment in Britain’s future that supports working households.”

News.title: 3 sisters who died off Brighton ‘never recovered’ from mum’s drowning death 16yrs before – as family say dad ‘catatonic’
News.content:
THE three sisters who died off Brighton beach “never recovered” from their mum’s death – as heartbroken relatives say their dad is “catatonic”.

“Inseperable” Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, were tragically pulled from the water last Wednesday.





The sisters – who lived together in Uxbridge, West London – were swept away at sea after entering the water at around 5.30am.

It is feared they were “suddenly dragged into danger after misjudging the shingle shelf” near the water’s edge, but a police probe remains ongoing.

And the tragedy comes 16 years after the death of their mum Janice, 43, who also sadly died by drowning in Brookvale Park lake in Birmingham.

She went missing in January 2010 – when the sisters were aged 20, 16 and 15 – and their aunt Ajike Adetoro, said the girls “never recovered”.

Ajike, known as Auntie Jik to the sisters, also said their dad Joseph, 68, is completely “catatonic” with grief in the wake of his daughter’s deaths.

She told MailOnline: “They are his babies. He is a softie anyway. My brother is a teddy bear, but when it comes to his girls… He has been catatonic.”

His partner and the girls’ step-mother Genevieve Barnaby-Adetoro said Joseph has been struggling to sleep and eat following the tragedy.

She told how the couple had been watching the news when the bodies were pulled from the sea, unaware it was their girls who had been found.



They did not know the sisters had been in Brighton until Joseph received a phone call from police asking about his children.

Officers later arrived at their London home and informed them in person, before they travelled to the south coast to identify the bodies.

It has also heavily affected their half-sister, Lilly, 25, who has reportedly been “inconsolable” following the tragedy.



Genevieve says the heartbroken family are trying to get Lilly, who is currently living out in America, back to the UK for the funeral.

She continued: “We think it’s right that Lilly is involved. We’ve said she can be in charge of their homecoming. We will ask her to pick their clothes.

“She wants it to be as beautiful as possible, with white caskets and white roses. She even wants a carriage to take them home… to honour them.”

But the relatives are still waiting to set a date for the funeral, with cops yet to release the girls’ bodies.

Ajike is desperate for answers, with the investigation to understand how exactly Jane, Christina and Rebecca came to be in the water still ongoing.



She continued: “I pray that they’ve been being mischievous, that one of them lost their footing and the others dived in to save them.

“Did one fall in and the others go to help, because they would have done… We are their family, and we don’t have answers.”

Eldest sister Jane, who worked as an accountant, took on the “role of mother” to her younger siblings Christina and Rebecca.

Christina had recently graduated from Brunel University, while Rebecca was described as the “baby” of the family, who was mischievous and lively.

The pebbled beach around Brighton and the Palace Pier is notorious for steep slopes, which can be incredibly dangerous for swimmers.



Releasing a tribute through Sussex Police, Joseph hailed his daughters as “my joy and my strength”.

It read: “Today, with a heart full of sorrow and love, I pay tribute to my beloved daughters whose lives ended so tragically far too soon.

“No words can truly describe the pain of losing three daughters in the prime of their lives.

“Jane, Christina, and Becky were more than daughters to me; they were my joy, my strength, and the beautiful light that filled our family with happiness and love.

“Each of you was unique and precious in your own special way.



“Your smiles brightened dark days, your laughter brought comfort, and your presence made life more meaningful.

“Though your time on earth was short, the impact you made will remain in our hearts forever.”

The force said there is currently no evidence to suggest third-party involvement or criminality.

Chief Superintendent Adam Hays, Divisional Commander for Brighton and Hove urged anyone with information to come forward.

He said: “The thoughts of everyone at Sussex Police are with the family of Jane, Christina and Rebecca following this devastating loss.



“I know this incident has had a profound impact on the local community in Brighton and across the country.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’d like to reassure the public we will leave no stone unturned in our investigation to understand exactly what led to the tragic events of that Wednesday morning.

“This investigation will continue in earnest, with Jane, Christina and Rebecca’s family at its centre.”

News.title: Dover border chaos as FOUR HOURS of queues at port force France to suspend extra EU border checks
News.content:
RIGHT ON QUEUE Dover border chaos as FOUR HOURS of queues at port force France to suspend extra EU border checks

MOTORISTS are facing chaos at the Port of Dover as they face four hours of queues.

New EU border checks at Dover have been suspended as drivers queue for hours amid climbing temperatures at the start of a hot bank holiday weekend.





Holidaymakers faced hours-long waits on Friday at the Port of Dover and travellers on Saturday came up against similar disruption.

In a bid to ease congestion, the French authorities suspended extra EU border checks under its new entry/exit system (EES) following the “challenging situation,” the port announced.

“While conventional border checks will still be undertaken, this will now enable Police Aux Frontieres (PAF) to significantly reduce the border processing time,” it said.

“We will be working with PAF and all out partners to get customers into and through the port as swiftly as possible and keep the roads clear for our local community.”

It also said anyone who has missed their ferry crossing because of queues can travel on the next available slot free of charge.

EES involves people from third-party countries such as the UK having their fingerprints registered and photograph taken to enter the Schengen Area, which consists of 29 European countries, mainly in the EU.



More than 8,000 travellers are expected at the port throughout Saturday.

Before the Bank Holiday weekend, the Port warned ferry passengers to expect long queues and possible delays due to the checks.

It said it was preparing for 18,000 travellers between Friday and Sunday, and warned that the busiest periods each day will be between 6am and about 1pm.

There were already hour-long processing waits at border control by 6am yesterday morning.

Passengers are being advised to use the main road routes to the port, arrive no earlier than two hours before departure and ensure they have a confirmed booking and all travel documents ready.



Travellers are also being told to prepare for possible delays by bringing food and water.

Meanwhile, long queues could be seen for the Euro Tunnel along the M20 in Folkestone, Kent on Saturday as the long weekend getaway continues.

It comes amid what is expected to be a sweltering May bank holiday weekend.

According to the Met Office, records could be broken for the the hottest May day in the UK and England, the hottest May day in Wales, as well as the UK and England’s hottest bank holiday.

Highs of 30C are likely to be recorded in the south of England today after the UK saw the hottest day of the year so far on Friday while peaks of 31C are expected on Sunday.



The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued amber heat health alerts on Friday morning for the East Midlands, West Midlands, the east of England, London and the South East.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The alerts will remain in place until 5pm on Wednesday and replace less severe yellow alerts which were previously issued.

The alerts mean there is likely to be “a rise in deaths, particularly among those aged 65 and over or with health conditions” and increased demand on all health and social care services, according to the UKHSA website.

News.title: M40 carnage after ‘multi-vehicle’ crash on motorway as drivers hit with 4 miles of queues & delays of 45 minutes
News.content:
A MULTI-vehicle collision is causing huge delays for bank holiday travellers on a major motorway.

Motorists have reported four mile long congestion queues after a crash at around 11:30am.



Police shut two lanes on the M40 Southbound between junction 10 Ardley and junction 9 Bicester.



Fire crews were called to the crash just before 12pm which resulted in four miles of congestion and 45 minute delays

National Highways East has reported the vehicles have been moved to the hard shoulder and the lanes re opened.

However motorists still face residual delays of 60 minutes and five miles of congestion.

News.title: Horror as mum, 42, plunges 2,000ft into a volcano on birthday hike after slipping while taking a pic
News.content:
HIKING TRAGEDY Horror as mum, 42, plunges 2,000ft into a volcano on birthday hike after slipping while taking a pic

A 42-YEAR-OLD mum of two has died after falling 2,000ft into a volcano during a birthday hike.

The climber was taking photos when she lost her grip and plummeted to her death.





Ingrid Daniela Vera Figueroa was climbing the Llaima Volcano, one of the largest and most active volcanoes in Chile, with a group of friends.

The mum of two had posted a message on social media just hours before she fell to her death.

Ingrid said: “It’s three in the morning and we’re finishing packing our backpacks to ascend Llaima.

“I hope God accompanies me on this wonderful day, on which I’m turning 42 and am super happy.”

In an ominous end to the message, she added: “Yes, I have a little uncertainty about what’s going to happen.”

The horror accident happened on Sunday May 17.

Ingrid was reportedly taking pictures as she descended the volcano.

She had reportedly released her ice pick and lost her balance in strong winds.



The mum then slipped and fell into the volcano to her death from around 2,000ft.

Rescue efforts were hampered by severe weather – powerful winds stopped a helicopter from being able to reach the mum.

Ingrid’s death was confirmed that same evening but her body could not be recovered until the next day because of the brutal conditions.



National Forest Corporation director Héctor Tillería said the hiking group hadn’t registered with the park authorities before embarking on their climb.

He warned other walkers of further extreme weather this week, including sub-zero temperatures.

Héctor urged all climbers to register properly with authorities for safety.

A school spokesperson, where Ingrid served as governor, called her a “responsible, kind, committed” mother.

The community offered condolences to her husband, two children, family and friends.



An investigation has been opened into Ingrid’s tragic death.

News.title: We forked out £4,200 on ‘five-star’ holiday in Brit holiday hotspot… then deadly bug left our baby with 10 hours to live
News.content:
IT was the holiday of a lifetime for parents Megan and Alex Crook – who forked out £4,200 for a plush all-inclusive resort in Egypt for their two teenage kids and toddler.

But the dream trip turned into a nightmare when two-year-old Chloe fell ill, with deadly E. coli, and was left fighting for her life for months.



Now, the Kent couple tell The Sun of their trauma and the road back to a normal life for “warrior” Chloe.

The holiday, in July 2024, was booked through TUI UK Limited and the family spent their stay by the Red Sea at the luxury, five star Jaz Makadi Aquaviva hotel.

Several popular holiday operators sell trips to the hotel – including easyJet Holidays, loveholidays, Thomas Cook and Holiday Hypermarket.



Megan said her first impressions of the Jaz Makadi Aquaviva were very positive.

She told The Sun: “It looked stunning. It took your breath away.”

But their initial opinion was not long-lived.

The Crooks say they found soiled sheets left dumped in the rooms, birds flying around the food and a worrying gremlin in the energy grid.

They claimed that the hotel suffered multiple power cuts throughout the day, with the electricity off for 40 minutes at a time.



When Chloe first started complaining one evening, her parents attributed it to a long day and the fact that she’d been playing outside in the heat.

But they quickly realised something was desperately wrong when she began vomiting in the middle of the night.

The power cuts went from being an irritating inconvenience to a major health hazard.



Megan said: “Obviously you’ve got a very, very poorly child that I’m keeping in the room to keep her temperature down. But the air con wouldn’t be working for 40 minutes. So the room would heat back up.

“It also left us wondering what was going on with the fridges.”

Alex added: “It is actually extremely dangerous to keep turning the fridge on and off, because it creates dangerous toxins which are linked to E. coli.”

Chloe’s health began rapidly deteriorating, and she experienced diarrhoea, vomiting, fever and fatigue while her parents fought to keep her cool.

With her symptoms worsening, she was rushed to a clinic, but the family claim they were met with a familiar obstacle.



Alex said: “Money, money, money. That was the priority.”

A doctor then gave Chloe anti-sickness and diarrhoea medication, along with an intravenous drip. The tot stopped vomiting, but the Crooks have been left to wonder whether this would eventually do more harm than good.

Sharon said: “We look at it now and with the strand of E.coli O157 that she got [and think] is that quite dangerous to give them anti-sickness and anti-diarrhoea medication? Because you’re trapping the E. coli in your body.”



The situation went from bad to worse when they discovered blood in Chloe’s nappy and she was rushed to hospital on July 6, 2024.

“It went downhill very quickly,” recalled Megan.

The parents experienced helpless terror as their daughter became desperately ill.

“There was a point in the hospital where they had to fly two surgeons in from Cairo to start dialysis,” Megan remembered.

“And they told us if they don’t do dialysis now, she has around 10 hours left to live.



“She wasn’t talking anymore. She was having seizures.”

Tests showed that her kidneys had started to fail while she was having emergency dialysis and she was diagnosed with Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome caused by E. coli infection.

Chloe’s parents then began “frantically” searching for hospitals so that she could be repatriated.



The Crooks were given a lifeline when Evelina London Children’s Hospital stepped in and offered a bed to Chloe.

The family’s insurers, Allianz, immediately arranged flights for them to Luton, after which Chloe was airlifted to London.

“She had 19 specialists waiting for her. Brain and kidney doctors,” Alex said.

They put Chloe into a coma for four days, to give her brain a “rest” and check for any damage.

Her kidneys had stopped working, so doctors had to urgently insert another central line – to draw out blood into a dialysis machine and return it cleaned – into her neck.



And fortunately, Chloe pulled through the coma.

“We didn’t realise the enormity of her waking back up, because if she had been brain damaged, we would have been full- time carers for the rest of our lives,” Sharon said.

Chloe’s parents were astounded by their daughter’s strength of character.

Alex said: “We’re extremely proud of her. It’s something that neither of us felt like we could have done ourselves.

“But she is an extremely determined and stubborn child, potentially her superpower, because she took back control of her left lung from the coma machine, which set the alarms off.



“She’s incredibly strong and resilient.”

Megan added: “She’s a warrior. An absolute warrior.”

The couple say they are incredibly grateful to the “amazing people” at Evelina and to Ronald McDonald House for being a “lifeline” and giving them free accommodation while they took shifts being at Chloe’s bedside.

The toddler was discharged from hospital on July 31, and still has to attend follow‑up appointments with the hospital’s nephrology (kidney) team.

The hotel and TUI were informed of Chloe’s situation in the resort, and were able to support the family throughout the ordeal. The family was offered a full refund as a gesture of goodwill, which they declined.



TUI say they are looking into the case, and The Sun has contacted Jaz Hotels for comment.

Six-year-old Arthur Broughton also contracted HUS on a £2,400 holiday to the same hotel – and has been left with life-altering health problems.

Sharon Turner and Daniel Broughton set off on their dream week-long, all-inclusive family trip to Egypt, last August, full of anticipation.

Sharon explained that “happy-go-lucky” Arthur was over the moon to be in Africa, which he describes as “his favourite continent”.

But unlike the Crooks, they were immediately shocked by the state of the hotel.



Sharon claimed: “The room was absolutely disgusting to the point where they said they cleaned it three times, and I said to them, ‘Look, I don’t want to be that person, but give me the cleaning things and I’ll clean it myself’.”

The couple, who booked the holiday through TUI, told a company rep that they felt that they had been missold on the hotel’s five star rating.

They claim they were told that Egypt operates under a different hotel star system, where reviews influence the rating.

They also criticised the response of a TUI employee who they complained to and felt that they were not taken seriously, and didn’t know if their complaints were ever escalated.

TUI said it was informed of the concerns about cleanliness and arranged for a deep clean of their room, and they also offered a hotel move at an additional cost.



The couple declined the offer and decided they weren’t going to let the disappointment ruin their trip, especially as Arthur was so excited to be there.

But hygiene remained a cause for concern.

“When you’d walk back to your room, a lot of bedrooms had plates of things like rice and chips because so many people were ill in their room,” Daniel claimed.

Sharon said they were talking to another family whose children had been ill for more than half of their twelve day holiday.

What is Haemolytic Uraemic Syndrome? HAEMOLYTIC Uraemic Syndrome (HUS) is a rare but serious medical condition that primarily affects the blood, blood vessels, and kidneys. It can sometimes lead to the destruction of red blood cells, a low platelet count, and acute kidney failure and in worst cases, death. It is most commonly triggered by a severe bacterial infection of the digestive tract, though there are other rarer causes. In most cases, a person develops it after catching E. coli which comes from contaminated food or water. Symptoms include severe abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhea, pale skin, bruising, swelling and fatigue. HUS usually develops around five to ten days after symptoms first show. Those suffering are often taken to hospital and given kidney dialysis if their organs are showing signs of failure. HUS can be deadly but in most cases it can be treated if caught early enough.

Sharon alleged: “It’s the first hotel I’ve been to where you don’t see any cleaning products. You don’t see any spray bottles. They used old towels from the hotel ripped up and wrapped around things to wipe up.



“They use mops that were just black. It looked like something you’d see on a garage floor in a mechanics garage.

“Even Centre Parcs was cleaner than this.”

Arthur initially developed what his parents believed was a mild stomach bug during the trip, before his condition rapidly deteriorated on the journey home.

Daniel said the six-year-old was “constantly back and forth to the toilet” at the airport and throughout the overnight flight to the UK, with the family rushing him to the bathroom every few minutes.

Within days of returning home, Arthur was admitted to hospital with HUS after his kidneys failed.



He was later transferred to Manchester Children’s Hospital, where he underwent dialysis for 12 days and spent time in intensive care after doctors feared he may have suffered a brain bleed.

Heartbreakingly, Sharon recalled Arthur telling her: “I don’t want to die. I don’t think I’m going to get better Mummy.”

The couple said the speed at which the illness progressed left them terrified.

Arthur temporarily lost the ability to walk properly and struggled with slurred speech and coordination after leaving intensive care.

But the six-year-old was able to relearn to stand and walk on trips around the hospital ward and back at home.



Sharon said: “The boy just shines. He really does.”

Arthur has since returned to school but continues to suffer ongoing kidney problems and requires regular hospital appointments and blood tests.

His parents said the ordeal has also left him with anxiety about travelling abroad again.

Sharon said: “There’s a worry monster in school and on Friday he put a worry in the worry monster about getting sick on holiday again.”

The family praised staff at Manchester Children’s Hospital for saving Arthur’s life and supporting them throughout the ordeal.



“That hospital is amazing,” Sharon said.

“The NHS has saved his life. There’s no two ways about it.

“Every time I hang his coat up, every time I complain about his school shoes in the hallway, I know I am lucky that he’s there because of everything that they did.”

Jatinder Paul, the lawyer representing the two families, said: “The fact these incidents have occurred at the same Egyptian hotel is a major cause for concern.

“While nothing can undo the ordeal these families have suffered, our focus is now on helping to provide them with the answers they deserve and either the specialist support they require to come to terms with their loss or the specialist rehabilitation these children now need.”



TUI commissioned an independent investigation at the Jaz Makadi Aquaviva hotel, including on-site assessments and hygiene and food safety testing, and did not identify E. coli.

Since 2022, TUI has taken around 80,000 customers to this hotel, and says reported illness levels remaining low at approximately 0.3 per cent.

TUI encourages customers to report illness while on holiday wherever possible so appropriate support can be provided.

Based on TUI’s internal reporting data, reported illness levels in Egypt are low overall – around 0.29 per cent – and are in line with levels seen in other popular destinations.

Over many years, TUI, together with the UK travel industry, has worked in partnership with Egyptian authorities and hotel partners to help strengthen health, safety and hygiene standards.



This includes supporting industry guidance, training and ongoing improvements designed to protect both international travellers and those working within the destination.

UKHSA continuously monitors international health risks and updates its advice where needed.

For example, it issued specific guidance to UK travellers in July 2019 following cases of E. coli linked to Hurghada in Egypt.

TUI maintains ongoing engagement with UKHSA and FCDO, and operates in line with official guidance on destination health, safety and travel advice.

TUI said in a statement: “We are also very sorry to hear about the serious illnesses experienced by Arthur and Chloe, and the effect this has had on them and their families. We appreciate how frightening such experiences can be.



“Reports of illness, particularly involving children, are taken extremely seriously.

“We continue to monitor any reports of illness in line with our routine process alongside the hotel, local authorities and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and full cooperation is being given to all relevant investigations.

“It would not be appropriate to speculate on cause while these processes are ongoing.

“Customers with health concerns during or following their holiday are encouraged to seek medical advice and to contact our customer support team so that assistance can be offered.”

News.title: Fears Brit tourists at risk as Somali pirates expand reign of terror with cruise ship attacks among chilling new tactics
News.content:
ARMED TO THE TEETH Fears Brit tourists at risk as Somali pirates expand reign of terror with cruise ship attacks among chilling new tactics

ARMED to the teeth with AK-47s, Somali pirates are advancing with new tactics and “military” training as they expand their reign of terror, experts say.

Holidaymakers enjoying cruises are coming under threat – with luxury vessels attacked and even boarded by terrifying gangs.





Pirates have launched seven attacks on vessels off the African coast since February – including four hijackings in quick succession off the Puntland coast in late April.

Pirates are currently holding 10 crew members of an Indonesian-flagged vessel hostage after invading the ship last month.

And vicious gangs are demanding a $10million ransom for the release of the Togo-flagged MT Eureka and its crew, hijacked off the coast of Yemen on May 2.

Hijackings of vessels by Somali pirate gangs were once commonplace around the Gulf of Aden and Indian Ocean, a ​major shipping lane used to transport energy and goods.

They eased through much of last year – but incidents are ​on the rise again, and now they are advancing, experts say.

The hijack of the MT Eureka tanker reportedly involved 30 armed pirates.

Expert Christopher Hockey told The Sun: “Attacks historically did not involve such large groups.

“The vessel appears to have been anchored, but was taken towards Somalia after being hijacked.



“This is also unusual. Incidents involving Somali pirates on this side of the Gulf of Aden have not really been reported before.”

The resurgence comes amid the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea as the US-Israeli war with Iran rages on.

Pirates are now exploiting this distraction to attack ships as they reroute around Africa to avoid active conflict zones, experts say.



Khadija Mamouni, from the Policy Centre for the New South, told The Sun that pirates have enhanced their attacks with technology – now operating drones and using GPS systems to track ships.

Mamouni said Somali piracy is “mutating” into an “high-precision industry”.

Pirates are now teaming up with military rebel groups like Iran-backed Houthis and al-Shabaab, using skiffs and new tech to strike ships with coordination not seen in a decade.

During the war in Gaza, the Houthis wreaked havoc on international shipping in the Red Sea.

Last July, the world witnessed the group sink two giant cargo ships within days of one another, causing sea traffic to drop and insurance costs to soar.



These alliances mean pirate groups are not only benefiting from arms smuggling but also military training, Mamouni said.

Dhows – traditional wooden vessels – are hijacked by pirates and used as “motherships” to move seamlessly through maritime traffic.

They shoot high-speed skiffs towards their target vessels, threatening the ship with rocket-propelled grenades and rifles, before using ladders to board.



And it’s not just cargo ships at risk – with the threat posed to cruise ships exposed last year.

Holidaymakers aboard Cunard’s Queen Anne were told to turn off their cabin lights and avoid outside decks as they sailed through a notorious area of the Philippines.

An announcement on board warned passengers: “This area is known for piracy threats, therefore we will be operating at a heightened level of security alertness.“

There have been six reported attacks on cruise ships since 2005, with the latest in 2012 and the majority in Somali waters.

Donna Meads-Barlow was on MSC Melody with her husband and three children in April 2009 when the cruise director announced: “We are under attack by pirates.”



Passengers on the ship sailing off the coast of Somalia were ordered to stay in their cabin, close their curtains and turn lights out.

“Please don’t panic, help is on its way,” the announcement said.

Donna told The Telegraph: “We could hear a heck of a commotion going on outside in the corridors of our cabin.



“And what was even more scary was that we didn’t know if the pirates had boarded and taken control of our ship… we lay there for hours and held hands so tight that we almost cut off circulation.”

The next morning the ship was the scene of a nightmare – with windows shattered by bullet holes.

Eight balaclava clad pirates had tried to board the ship and opened fire with AK-47 rifles.

Security guards fired eight shots into the air and let off two emergency flares to scare them away while some of the 1,200 passengers hurled tables and chairs down at them.

“It was like war,” Captain Ciro Pinto said. A Spanish warship eventually arrived to escort MSC Melody from the area.



That same year Brit couple Paul and Rachel Chandler were sailing off the coast of the Seychelles in their 38ft yacht, Lynn Rival, when they were shot at by eight Somali pirates in the dead of night.

The armed mercenaries climbed aboard and kidnapped them, first taking them to the previously hijacked merchant ship MV Kota Wajar and then to land, were they were held for 388 agonising days.

The terrified couple were eventually released after a reported £600,000 ransom was paid to their captors.



Now it’s feared more holidaymakers could be at risk as the pirates return with stronger force.

Piracy is driven by strong financial incentives, with profits from ransoms or stolen goods divvied up between pirates, local authorities, sponsors and transnational criminal actors.

The danger posed by piracy off the coast of Somalia extends beyond attacks on shipping, Mamouni warned.

She said: “This area is a highly militarised region, where navies have inadequate monitoring capacities and lack enforcement abilities.

“The Horn of Africa’s onshore and offshore insecurity is all connected, from the civil war in Sudan and al-Shabaab’s terror attacks in East Africa to instability in Yemen.”



History of piracy on the coast of Somalia The so-called “Golden Age of Piracy” might have ended with the 18th century – but daring raids at sea have become a constant menace once again in the new millennium. An explosion of piracy in the Gulf of Aden off the Somali coast in the 2000s brought the issue sharply into international attention. Hijackings escalated as the Somali government collapsed during the Somali-Ethiopia war of 2006-09. Fishermen from Somali coastal communities responded by arming themselves to protect local resources. Thousands of ships were captured or fired at with pirates demanding millions of dollars in ransoms. By 2010, Somali waters had become the most pirate-infested in the world, accounting for 92 per cent of the 53 ships captured worldwide that year. The World Bank estimated that from 2005 to 2012, ransoms totalled between $339million and $413million. An international coalition composed of NATO’s Operation Ocean Shield, EUNAVFOR Operation Atalanta, the Combined Maritime Task Force, and the Somali authorities began patrolling the area. The patrols and the 47-country naval partnership helped to reduce attacks drastically.

Piracy is now part of a wider system of “transnational organised crime”, she said.

Somali piracy first emerged out of frustrated fishing communities who accused foreign vessels of plundering their fisheries.

But they soon found taking over foreign ships and demanding ransoms was a highly profitable racket, and they gained backing from former militiamen looking to make money from the emerging crime.

Pirates waged a brutal war on cargo ships throughout the 2010s before their threat was subdued.



But the root cause was not addressed, allowing groups to retreat and rearm before the current resurgence.

Now a “massive challenge” lies ahead for authorities, senior researcher at Transnational Threats and Organised Crime Timothy Walker told The Sun.

A lack of effective governance, complex clan dynamics, corruption and economic instability continue to blight Somalia.

Illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing in Somali territorial waters also continues, sparking frequent attacks.

Walker said: “Maritime insecurity for coastal communities, and with it food and job insecurity is increasing in coastal Somalia.



“Near-collapse of sea-dependent livelihoods with few alternative income options, may increasing the appeal of piracy.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The recent attacks should be seen “as a warning that the western Indian Ocean’s maritime order remains fragile”.

He added: “Whether this becomes the beginning of a more sustained piracy cycle will depend on whether regional and international actors treat Somalia’s maritime insecurity as a long-term governance challenge rather than only a naval problem.”

News.title: Armed police shoot man in Whitefield getaway bid as gun and drugs found
News.content:
Armed police shoot man in Whitefield getaway bid as gun and drugs found

Police pursuing a vehicle in Whitefield said the driver failed to stop and drove directly at officers to get away, before he was shot in the arm and taken to hospital

View 2 Images Forensic officers attend the scene in Whitefield (Image: Getty Images)

A man was shot by armed cops after he drove at them during a dramatic getaway attempt in Whitefield, with drugs and a gun later recovered by detectives.

Greater Manchester Police said officers tried to stop a car on Bury New Road at around 3pm on Friday, but the driver "failed to stop and drove directly at officers to get away". A firearms officer then discharged a weapon, striking the 20-year-old man in the arm.

He was taken to hospital with injuries described as neither life-threatening nor life-changing, while the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) later said he had suffered a suspected broken elbow.

Detectives later recovered drugs and a gun, and the man was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of Class A drugs.

View 2 Images Forensic officers search the scene (Image: Getty Images)

In an update, GMP said an investigation into the incident is ongoing. The force said officers searched an address in Radcliffe overnight and found a firearm and a "significant" quantity of both Class A and Class B drugs. No further arrests have been made.

Detective Superintendent Joe Harrop, from GMP's Serious Crime Division said: "Our officers were met with an extremely dangerous situation on Bury New Road yesterday. Thankfully no members of the wider public, or officers were harmed in the incident.

"Despite this, our team has acted swiftly and professionally, and our investigation has progressed at pace. Overnight searches have led to the recovery of a firearm and a significant quantity of Class A and B drugs. This is a substantial find and it in turn prevents a potentially dangerous weapon and a significant amount of drugs from reaching our streets.

Article continues below

"Our investigation will progress, and we will continue to target those involved in serious and organised crime to keep our communities safe for all those who live and work across the whole of Greater Manchester."

In a statement issued this morning, the IOPC said: "We are independently investigating following a non-fatal police shooting in Bury. We were made aware by Greater Manchester Police, who advised that a man was shot in the arm after a vehicle failed to stop for officers. He was taken to hospital with a suspected broken elbow.

"While firearms incidents like this are, thankfully, rare, it is important for there to be independent scrutiny to fully understand what has happened. IOPC investigators attended the scene and to the police post-incident procedures to begin gathering evidence."

News.title: Young people are being failed by 'shameful' welfare system
News.content:
Young people are 'being failed by shameful' welfare system

Former health secretary Alan Milburn claimed his review found the state was spending 25 times more on welfare for young people than on measures to get them into jobs

View 2 Images Alan Milburn claimed the state was spending 25 times more on welfare for young people than on measures to get them into jobs (Image: In Pictures via Getty Images)

The state has failed young people in a “shameful” way by “transporting them into the world of benefits”, the leader of a major Government review has warned.

‌



Former health secretary Alan Milburn claimed his review found the state was spending 25 times more on welfare for young people than on measures to get them into jobs.

‌



Mr Milburn also hit out at the impact of social media on young people’s lives which had fuelled anxiety and “rewired” their brains.

‌



Appearing on BBC ’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg, he said: “This is a failure of the welfare system, but it’s a failure – I’m sorry – of the school system, the skills system, the health system.

OPINION Alan Milburn, former Labour Health Secretary ALAN MILBURN: 'Young people are not lazy, distracted or entitled - we must not give up on them'

‌



View 2 Images Ex-Health Secretary Alan Milburn says we must not give up on young people

“What we’re doing is we’re not prioritising getting young people into a situation where they can be learning or earning. And instead we’re transporting them into the world of benefits with incalculable costs for their life chances.”

Asked what his message was to Labour about the need for welfare reform, he said: “Labour is what it says on the tin, it’s the party of work. Work gives purpose, work gives income, work gives meaning, it means you can contribute, but if you can’t do that, that has an impact, not least on your mental health, but also on your life chances.

Article continues below

“Second thing is, welfare reform is absolutely essential and needs to be done, but as I said it’s got to be within the context of a wider set of reforms to state institutions.”

Young people’s sleep patterns and concentration levels are being hurt by social media, the former health secretary warned, and “that is having an impact on their ability to work”.

Mr Milburn’s interim report into young Neets ( Not in Education Employment, or Training) is expected to be published next week. The total number of young people considered Neet is 957,000.

News.title: BBC The One Show's Amar Latif reveals terror of waking up blind aged 18
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: BBC The One Show's Amar Latif reveals terror of waking up blind aged 18

The One Show's Amar Latif may be blind, but that hasn't stopped him seeing the world. He's even set up his own travel company to do it, helping others living with disability too

View 4 Images Amar’s achievements earned him an OBE in 2023 for services to the visually impaired and entrepreneurship (Image: Ben Pearse Photography 2016)

The One Show presenter Amar Latif has ‘seen’ many wonders of the world - despite being blind. A documentary presenter, his shows include Travelling Blind with Sara Pascoe, Beyond Boundaries, Pilgrimage: The Road to Istanbul with Edwina Currie, Adrian Chiles and Fatima Whitbread and Myths and Legends with Jonathan Ross.

‌



For Amar, 51, refuses to let his disability restrict him. And, in 2004, when he couldn’t find a suitable travel firm, he started his own - Traveleyes. Amar, from Leeds, explains: “I couldn’t find a travel company that would allow me to see the world, so I set up my own one.

‌



“I offer fully sighted people half price travel and in return they become the eyes for the traveller who is blind. It means blind people get independence and freedom. Each day, our visually impaired person has a different sighted traveller acting as their eyes. One person might describe the buildings, another might describe the flora and fauna, so they get a different experience too. We’re supporting people to see the world in a different way.”

‌



One of five siblings, Amar was diagnosed with the rare, incurable genetic condition retinitis pigmentosa, causing visual impairment, aged 4. His younger sister and brother have it, too - but, like him, both have good jobs. Meanwhile, Amar’s achievements earned him an OBE in 2023 for services to the visually impaired and entrepreneurship.

View 4 Images Amar Latif points the way to Machu Picchu in Peru

Now from June 21 to 27 he will be presenting the BBC Radio 4 Appeal on behalf of the Rafiki Thabo Foundation. A 20-year-old charity where he’s a patron, it helps disadvantaged children and young people in East Africa to access education through scholarships. It’s helped nearly 1,000 people to study and has run a free school meals programme, improved school facilities, and worked to reduce barriers to education faced by children with disabilities.

‌



In August 2023, Amar trekked up Mount Kilimanjaro in aid of Rafiki Thabo, accompanied by sighted guides. Jon Uglow, founder of Rafiki Thabo Foundation says: "Amar is a hugely inspiring individual. It is a privilege to have him as a patron.”

Amar continues: “The Kilimanjaro trek was a big challenge. We did the final part at about 11pm, so a lot of the others had torches. I didn’t need one, so that was one advantage of being blind!”

Amar’s condition is caused by a recessive gene possessed by both his parents and he started losing his sight at school. He says: “My desk was moved to the front of the class. I was so self-conscious. I wore thick glasses and kids would tease me and say, ‘how many fingers am I holding up?’”

‌



View 4 Images Amar set up own travel firm Traveleyes in 2004

One night, aged 18, he says: “I went to bed as normal and the last thing I saw before I went to sleep was the poster of Madonna at the end of my bed. But when I woke up, I couldn’t see it.

“At first I thought it was morning fuzz, but it was complete whiteness.I felt claustrophobic and couldn’t breathe. I kept closing my eyes and opening them, hoping I would see my Madonna poster. I kept bumping into things. I couldn’t see the faces of my friends and family. I didn’t want to believe I was blind and thought my dreams of going to university and being an accountant were over.”

‌



Determined Amar got a pal to record their notes, so he could listen to them. Not only did he go to university, he spent a year studying in Canada - experiencing the beauty of the country through the descriptions given by friends.

He says: “I made amazing friends and we travelled together.” He went surfing in Hawaii with his brother, visited New York and Vancouver and skated on frozen canals. He says: “I wanted to travel more, but travel companies wouldn’t let me travel alone, or let alone do anything adventurous like sailing or rambling. The restrictions left me feeling powerless, so after university I set up Traveleyes.”

View 4 Images Pilgrimage: The Road to Istanbul, with Mim Shaikh, Pauline McLynn, Dom Joly, Edwina Currie, Adrian Chiles, Fatima Whitbread, Amar Latif (Image: BBC/CTVC/Oliver Rose)

‌



But Amar, who’s met people through Rafiki who’ve escaped desperate poverty through education, says he’s been blessed with opportunities. He says: “If I’d been born outside the UK, my blindness could’ve meant I ended up begging on the streets.

“Education has given me opportunities. I want to pay that forward to help others, which is why I’m so proud to support Rafiki Thabo. I might be blind but I’ve seen the world. I’ve been to Sri Lanka, Thailand, Morocco and Ghana. I went skydiving in Cuba. When the parachute opened, I felt like a bird. I remember being led to a helicopter. I could feel the wind and elements bombarding me from every side. I went ski-ing too. Someone in front wore a rucksack with music on and I followed the sound.”

But Amar’s had the odd disaster. He says: “I once crashed into a skip and somersaulted into the rubbish!” Amar also experiences preconceptions about blindness. He says: “Once a lady grabbed me by the arm and helped me cross a road I wasn’t planning to cross! And I’ve been approached by people who’ve asked if they can pray for me.” But he reacts with humour, saying: “After all, I’ve been able to do things I could never have dreamed of.

Article continues below

*To donate to Rafiki Thabo visit rafiki-foundation.org.uk

News.title: Aston Merrygold shares true feelings over X Factor after 'dangerous' success with JLS
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Aston Merrygold shares true feelings over X Factor after 'dangerous' success with JLS

JLS star and dad-of-three Aston Merrygold recalls the 'dangerous' early days of fame, and tells of his sorrow at fellow X Factor alum Liam Payne's tragic death at 31

View 6 Images Singer and actor Aston Merrygold of JLS (Image: Grant Buchanan/Dave Benett/Getty Images for Make-A-Wish UK)

Shooting to fame with JLS on X Factor, former boyband star Aston Merrygold, says he was once in the “exact same space” as One Direction’s Liam Payne. Runners up to Alexander Burke on the 2008 show, JLS had formed the previous year in London, but the TV show made them stars.

‌



Aston, 38, says:“I was 20 when I appeared on X Factor. It would have been very easy to go off the rails. The things that are thrown at you, given to you, the doors that are open. Your best interests aren't always going to be at the forefront of things.

‌



“When you look at someone like Liam and the rest of the One Direction boys, we were in the exact same space at one point. And our paths crossed, of course they did. From the outside it's all very shiny, life looks incredible but it's scary. It's scary to think of how Liam was feeling.

‌



6 View 6 Images Liam Payne, of boyband One Direction, who died in 2024 (Image: Getty Images for ABA) 6 View 6 Images Aston and Liam were both on the X Factor, ITV's juggernaut talent show (Image: Getty Images for Warner Bros.)

“As a kid, you're given the opportunities to be standing center stage in front of thousands of people. They've bought a ticket. There's money that goes into that ticket that goes into several people's pockets including yours. That can turn into a lot of money, and a lot of success at a young age. That's very dangerous.”

Aston was rocked by the news of Liam’s death in October 2024, after the 31-year-old singer fell from a third-floor balcony in Argentina, while high on drugs The tragedy happened 9 years after 1D - which also featured Niall Horan, Harry Styles, Louis Tomlinson and Zayn Malik - split up, having sold more than 70 million records worldwide since being formed on the 2010 X Factor.

‌



JLS - which also includes Marvin Humes, now 41, JB Gill 39, and Oritsé Williams, 39 - have sold more than 10million records worldwide and had 5 UK number ones. And the band is now enjoying a renaissance, with a string of sold out shows coming up this summer.

But Aston, who lives in Hertfordshire with his wife, Sarah, 42, a dancer and choreographer, and their three children, Grayson, eight, Macaulay, five, and Riley, two, says life in the spotlight is very different now.

6 View 6 Images Aston, his wife Sarah, and their three children, Grayson, eight, Macaulay, five, and Riley, two (Image: Alan West/Hogan Media/Shutterstock) 6 View 6 Images Sarah Merrygold and Aston Merrygold attend the 2026 BAFTA Television Awards with P&O Cruises at The Royal Festival Hall on May 10, 2026 in London (Image: Getty Images for BAFTA)

‌



The star - who has just voiced an audiobook for Bupa Dental Care, The Dentist’s Apprentice, by Jennifer Gray, which is designed to help kids understand the dentist - says: “When I appeared on X Factor I was 20 - four years older than Liam.

“It’s early adulthood, you don't really know what's happening in life. My best friends in the world were still in uni, getting battered every weekend, while I was flying across the world. You're not guided in any way, you're just kind of thrown out there. It’s, ‘you want to be an entertainer - go do it’. As a child you're always going to be attracted to the sparkly shiny stuff.

"It's a very tempting but dangerous industry in that sense. And for life to just be kind of taken away like that [of Liam] is just heartbreaking for his friends, family, son. As a dad now, you go, ‘Oh my god’. It gives you shivers. The life we embarked on is such a whirlwind.”

‌



After splitting in 2013 and playing a farewell concert at London’s O2 Arena that December, the JLS lads released a greatest hits album and then pursued solo careers. But they reunited in 2020 and Aston says: “I’m so grateful to be able to come back and do it as an adult and get a second chance.

View 6 Images JLS: Marvin Humes, Aston Merrygold, JB Gill and Oritse Williams (Image: UK)

“In our industry, you grow up fast and you have to have thick skin. Everything is being watched on a massive microscope. It's daunting. But I've learned over the years that it's the entertainment industry, it's really not that serious. I'm not doing heart transplants or brain surgery.

Article continues below

“Fame's cool and money's great, but there are a lot more valuable things in life. And these days, my rider is mainly full of snacks for my kids!”

News.title: Pensioners may not realise they could boost income to £18,500 a year
News.content:
Pensioners may not realise they could boost income to £18,500 a year

Pensioners aged 66 or over with a long-term illness or disability could be eligible for this tax-free benefit

View 3 Images Older people on a low income or living with a health condition could be due extra financial help on top of their State Pension (Image: Getty)

Many of the 13 million pensioners in the UK may be unaware that they could qualify for additional tax-free benefits, potentially boosting their annual income to more than £18,500. Attendance Allowance and Pension Age Disability Payment (PADP) are not means-tested and will be worth either £3,988 or £5,959 this year.

‌



The full New State Pension is currently valued at £12,547, while the maximum Basic State Pension stands at £9,614. This means that anyone over 66 living with a long-term illness, disability or health condition could potentially pocket up to £18,506 a year, albeit through separate payments.

‌



As reported by the Daily Record, for those pensioners on a lower income, they may also qualify for Pension Credit, which could provide an additional £4,300 in financial support this year.

‌



The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) estimates that more than 700,000 people are entitled to Pension Credit, yet are failing to claim the income-related benefit.

Likewise, over one million pensioners are thought to be eligible for Attendance Allowance, which is unaffected by income or savings, is entirely tax-free and is not counted as income when applying for Pension Credit.

View 3 Images More than one million pensioners are believed to be eligible for Attendance Allowance (Image: Getty)

‌



Attendance Allowance and PADP

Attendance Allowance currently helps more than 1.7 million older people across England and Wales while 175,750 in Scotland are receiving extra support through PADP.

People over State Pension age claiming Attendance Allowance or PADP will receive either £76.70 (lower rate) or £114.60 (higher rate) each week. As the benefit is usually paid every four weeks, this amounts to either £306.80 or £458.40 every payment period - some £5,959.20 over the 2026/27 financial year.

Who can claim?

You should apply for Attendance Allowance or PADP if you have a disability or illness and need help or supervision throughout the day or at times during the night -even if you don’t currently get that help.

‌



This might include:

Help with your personal care - for example getting dressed, eating or drinking, getting in and out of bed, bathing or showering and going to the toilet

Help to stay safe

You should also apply if you have difficulties with personal tasks, for example if they take you a long time, you experience pain or you need physical help, like a chair to lean on. Attendance Allowance and PADP are not just for people with a physical disability or illness.

‌



You should also claim if you need help or supervision throughout the day or night and have:

a mental health condition

learning difficulties

a sensory condition - if you are deaf or visually impaired

Attendance Allowance and PADP are not means-tested so it doesn't matter what other money you have coming in or how much you have in savings either - there's no limit. it is also tax-free and you will be exempt from the Benefit Cap so you won't have money taken away from any other benefits you're already claiming.

‌



You can also claim it if you're still working and earning money.

How to make a claim

You will need to complete a long claim form when you apply for Attendance Allowance. It might seem daunting at first but help is available from Citizens Advice and Independent Age.

Full details of how to get the application form by post or over the phone can be found on the GOV.UK website here.

‌



To claim Pension Age Disability Payment, visit MYGOV.SCOT here.

Pension Credit

Pension Credit currently supports 1.4 million people, including 125,000 living in Scotland. It tops up weekly income to a guaranteed minimum level of £238.00 a week for single pensioners or £363.25 for couples. It is worth on average £4,300 this year.

If you are a single person on the New State Pension with a total weekly income below £238.00, or part of a couple with a combined weekly income of less than £363.25, you may be eligible for Pension Credit.

‌



An award of just £1 per week is enough to unlock access to other financial support, including Council Tax discounts and help with heating bills this winter through the Warm Home Discount Scheme.

Mixed aged older couples and Pension Credit

In May 2019, the law changed so a ‘mixed age couple’ - a couple where one partner is of State Pension age and the other is under it - are considered to be a ‘working age’ couple when checking entitlement to means-tested benefits.

This means they cannot claim Pension Credit or pension age Housing Benefit until they are both State Pension age. Before this DWP change, a mixed age couple could be eligible to claim the more generous State Pension age benefits when just one of them reached State Pension age.

‌



Other help if you get Pension Credit

If you qualify for Pension Credit you can also get other help, such as:

Housing Benefit if you rent the property you live in

Support for Mortgage Interest if you own the property you live in

Council Tax discount

Free TV licence if you are aged 75 or over

Help with NHS dental treatment, glasses and transport costs for hospital appointments

Help with your heating costs through the Warm Home Discount Scheme

A discount on the Royal Mail redirection service if you are moving house

View 3 Images The full, New State Pension is now worth £12,547 while the maximum Basic State Pension is worth £9,614 (Image: Getty)

‌



Quickest way to check eligibility for Pension Credit

Older people, or friends and family, can quickly check their eligibility and get an estimate of what they may receive by using the online Pension Credit calculator on GOV.UK here.

Alternatively, pensioners can contact the Pension Credit helpline directly to make a claim on 0800 99 1234 - lines are open 8am to 6pm, Monday to Friday.

Expert help and advice is also available from:

Article continues below

More details about claiming Pension Credit can be fond on GOV.UK here.

News.title: UK weather live: Heatwave maps forecast 35C surge with 15 counties at 33C – list
News.content:
Weather forecasting models suggest the UK could see temperatures rise to 35C as a heatwave grips the country - the Met Office has forecast 33C highs for Monday

Weather models show some parts of the country could see staggering temperatures of 35C on Tuesday.

It comes as the UK faces a days-long heatwave with the Met Office forecasting record breaking temperatures for May. Heat health alerts have been issued by the UKHSA across England.

The UKV weather model now suggests the East of England could reach 35C at around 3pm on Tuesday.
